meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's essay, Hale, and the zero you gave him.
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.

A machine's guess. Turnitin's own guide, which I have printed in my bag, says it "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student," and your procedure says the same thing. What else is there, besides software?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me what you actually have on the essay.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.

11:31, 11:52, 11:58, October 28; I'm writing those down. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, and pasting it in from somewhere else is what anyone does. That's a document being assembled, Hale, not proof of who wrote it.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.

Fine, he can produce that. Students misquote Shakespeare from memory all the time, so which edition is that, and is that line anywhere else in the play? Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.

You didn't answer me on that quotation, and I want the edition. As for the outline, students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's what outlines are for. Is that the only other writing of his you have?

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
Let me see those notes, Hale. A seventeen-year-old cornered by his teacher for five minutes says "like, being stuck"; that's nerves, not a confession. And I'm still waiting on that edition.

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Forty minutes in a classroom against a take-home essay; of course one is cleaner. Comma splices aren't evidence, and you still haven't given me that edition. So what are you actually putting on the table?

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

That's 4.4, private and in writing tonight, and we'll do it to put this behind him. His applications close December 1, so I want the rewrite date set this week and the new mark entered well before then. The edition on that quotation still goes in your email.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Okay. Thursday after school, marked within two days, and that goes in tonight's email with the rest. Who's supervising him, and where?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes. Who's supervising him and where goes in that email too. Ten minutes, Hale, so put it all in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will write a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, that it will be marked within two days, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require the edition you used for the quotation you say is not in Hamlet, and the name of the person supervising Owen and the room where he will write. I expect all of this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants all of it confirmed in writing tonight, along with the edition for the quotation and who will supervise; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached with time to spare.
What moved her: You turned your screen and walked her through the version history with exact times on the night of October 28, because it was specific, dated, tied to his own file and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You opened by saying the checker score meant the zero stood, which handed her the strongest argument she came in with and made you start over.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed on a late night in October, between 11:31 and 11:58 PM, very close to what she saw; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked which edition of the play you used for the missing quotation, name the edition right then, so that piece stands on its own instead of following you into her email.
